newsitem.title: USA: Jury begins deliberations on Texas murder.
newsitem.headline: Jury begins deliberations on Texas murder.

text.p: A jury began deliberations on Tuesday to decide whether Darlie Routier, convicted of one capital murder charge in the stabbing death of her two sons, should spend the rest of her life in prison or die by lethal injection.
Prosecutors urged the jury to give Routier the death penalty, but defence attorneys said she should be sent to prison for life, the only two sentencing options in a capital murder case.

Routier, 27, was found guilty on Saturday of killing her 5-year-old son, Damon. Another capital murder charge is pending in the death of Devon, 6. Both were stabbed to death with a butcher knife while they slept June 6 in their Rowlett, Texas, home near Dallas.

Capital murder is a more serious charge than murder and carries with it the possibility of a death sentence. If the jury orders Routier to die, she will become the seventh woman on Death Row in Texas prisons.

During Tuesday's arguments, prosecutor Greg Davis showed photographs of the dead boys to the seven-woman, five-man jury and told them she was a continuing threat to society, one of the grounds for giving the death penalty.
"This is a woman capable of the unspeakable in her own home," he said.
Another prosecutor, Sherri Wallace, said society must protect its children by punishing those who harm them.
"Darlie Routier, we are not going to tolerate what you have done to our children. You will die," she said.

Routier was composed through most of the proceedings but put her hands to her face and wept when defence attorney Richard Mosty, standing behind her with his hands on her shoulders, asked the jury for mercy. He said she was not guilty and not a threat to society.
"You know that whatever you found happened that night was a one-time event that's beyond explanation. There's no continuing threat to society," Mosty said.
Routier testified earlier in the trial that an intruder killed the boys and attacked her, but police said they found no evidence of that.

Prosecutors charged that Routier killed her sons in a fit of anger at the family's financial difficulties and her ongoing weight problems. They portrayed her as vain and selfish, which defence witnesses denied.
The trial, which began Jan. 6, was moved to Kerrville, 60 miles northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of heavy pre-trial publicity.
